title: Blondie (band)
wiki_lead:
Blondie is an American rock band formed in New York City in 1974 by singer Debbie Harry and guitarist Chris Stein. Emerging as a pioneer of the early new wave genre from the CBGB punk scene of the mid-1970s, the band subsequently achieved global commercial success with their third studio album, Parallel Lines (1978). The record launched a string of international hit singles, including "Heart of Glass", "Call Me", and "Rapture". Inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2006, the group has sold over 40 million records worldwide.
While Blondie's self-titled debut album, Blondie (1976), remained a strictly underground release, their second album, Plastic Letters (1978), brought the band their first commercial success in the United Kingdom and Australia. However, they remained largely unknown to mainstream audiences in their native United States until the release of their third studio album, Parallel Lines (1978). The record became an international breakthrough, selling an estimated 20 million copies worldwide. Over the next three years, the band achieved global chart dominance, releasing a string of hit singles through their follow-up albums Eat to the Beat (1979) and Autoamerican (1980). Their most successful tracks from this era included "Heart of Glass" (U.S. and U.K. No. 1), "One Way or Another", "Dreaming", "Call Me" (from the American Gigolo soundtrack; U.S. and U.K. No. 1), "Atomic", "The Tide Is High" (U.S. and U.K. No. 1), and "Rapture" (U.S. No. 1), which became the first "Billboard" number-one singles to feature rap vocals.
Blondie disbanded in late 1982 following the commercial failure of their sixth studio album, The Hunter (1982), which was compounded by internal tensions, financial difficulties, and the severe illness of co-founder and guitarist Chris Stein. Harry subsequently paused her career to care for Stein, who was diagnosed with pemphigus, a rare and life-threatening autoimmune disease of the skin. The band re-formed in 1997, achieving renewed success with their seventh album No Exit (1999) and their sixth number one single in the U.K. with "Maria" in 1999, exactly 20 years after their first U.K. number one single, "Heart of Glass".
The group toured and performed throughout the world during the following years, and was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2006. Blondie has sold over 40 million records worldwide and continues to actively perform. The band's eleventh studio album, Pollinator, was released on May 5, 2017, charting at number 4 in the U.K. A new studio album, High Noon, has been announced for release on February 26, 2027.

History


1974–1978: Early career
Inspired by the burgeoning new music scene at the Mercer Arts Center in Manhattan, musician Chris Stein sought a band with similar interests. He joined the Stilettoes in 1973 as their guitarist and formed a romantic relationship with Debbie Harry, who was one of the band's vocalists, a former waitress and Playboy Bunny. grok_lead: Blondie is an American rock band formed in New York City in 1974 by vocalist Debbie Harry and guitarist Chris Stein, emerging as pioneers of the new wave genre through their fusion of punk, pop, disco, and hip-hop elements. The band rose to global prominence in the late 1970s with multi-platinum albums like Parallel Lines (1978), which sold over 20 million copies worldwide, and chart-topping singles including "Heart of Glass," "Call Me," "The Tide Is High," and "Rapture," amassing four number-one hits on the Billboard Hot 100. After disbanding in 1982 amid internal tensions, Blondie reunited in 1997, achieving further success with the UK number-one single "Maria" from No Exit (1999) and continued releases such as Pollinator (2017), while selling more than 40 million records overall. Inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2006, the group remains active as of 2025, with a new studio album, High Noon, slated for release in spring 2026 featuring production by John Congleton and final recordings from late drummer Clem Burke, who passed away in April 2025. The band's original lineup included drummer Clem Burke, keyboardist Jimmy Destri, and bassist Gary Valentine, with early performances at iconic venues like CBGB shaping their raw, energetic sound amid New York's punk scene. Following their breakthrough, Blondie experimented across genresâincorporating reggae in "The Tide Is High," rap in "Rapture" (the first with a rapper to top the US charts), and electronic elementsâbefore their initial split due to exhaustion and personal challenges. The 1997 reunion revitalized their career, leading to six UK number-one singles in total, including "Atomic" and "Sunday Girl," and albums that blended nostalgia with modern production. As of 2025, Blondie's core creative force consists of Debbie Harry and Chris Stein, with Stein contributing primarily in the studio; the touring and recording lineup features bassist Leigh Foxx, keyboardist Matt Katz-Bohen, and guitarist Tommy Kessler. Their influence extends to fashion, MTV-era visuals, and gender dynamics in rock, with Harry's iconic image and versatile songwriting defining an era of boundary-pushing pop stardom. Despite lineup changes and the recent loss of Burke, Blondie persists as a enduring act, preparing what may be their final album while maintaining a legacy of innovation and commercial triumph.
